It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the "unsearchable riches" of Christ while witnessing the "noise and tumult" of a world where civil powers often seek to "exalt themselves above the assembly of the LORD," and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the boundaries of state authority and the plight of the stateless sojourner in this hour? [1, 13, 827, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling "overwhelmed and desperate" by the sight of "savage wolves" who "malign" the conscience of the believer, or are you seeking a "settled certainty" to anchor your soul in the truth that "history is His story"—a single, cohesive account of God’s glory that cannot be contained by any earthly "administrative order"? [13, 20, 21, 65, 835, 1143, 1301, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many "shave off the edges" of the truth to seek "diplomatic relations" with the culture, we must return to the "external Word" to see how the Master personally governs the "vicissitudes of life" by demanding that we "obey God rather than men" (Acts 5:29) [11, 28, 1057, 1503, 1529, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that "God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation," and therefore, the overstepping of a civil ruler into the realm of worship is not an "administrative anomaly" but evidence of a "rebellious heart" that God uses to prove that "His counsel shall stand, and He will do all His pleasure" (Isaiah 46:10) [15, 68, 1143, 1460, 1482, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Limits of Civil Jurisdiction**

**Verse**
“ ‘And He said to them, “Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s” ’ ” (Matthew 22:21). [1072, 1316, 1720, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that while "secular courts" are "appointed by God" for civil peace, their authority is strictly limited and "secondary" to the King of kings [835, 1228, 1519, Conversation History]. When a government demands that a church "register" to exist or attempts to "control the advance of His gospel," it is attempting to place itself in God's office, yet “the Word of God is not chained” by human paperwork (2 Timothy 2:9) [25, 41, 68, 1144, 1316, 1420, 1529, 1720, Conversation History]. We are commanded to be "loyal and submissive" in mundane civil matters, but we "refuse to yield submission" when the state tries to "tamper with or attempt to tone down the gospel" because "Jesus Christ alone is the head of the church" (Colossians 1:18) [19, 68, 116, 1144, 1316, 1500, 1528, 1636, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should "not be deceived" by those who suggest the state is the source of your "legitimacy," for "the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our Lawgiver, the LORD is our King; He will save us" (Isaiah 33:22) [15, 91, 1016, 1316, 1502, 1720, Conversation History]. "Trade in your worry for trust," recognizing that your "sole objective" is to find the "repose of the soul" in Christ's "finished work" rather than seeking "deliverance" from a "legislative body" (John 19:30; Psalm 62:2) [24, 51, 101, 130, 856, 1020, 1406, 1408, 1445, 1503, 1623, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the "theocracy" unified civil and religious law, but God still "removed kings from their thrones" when they "rejected the word of the LORD" to follow their own "ridiculous conceits" (1 Samuel 15:23) [7, 15, 17, 835, 1078, 1183, 1316, 1533, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by showing that the church is an "assembly of the citizens of heaven" whose "kingdom is not of this world," meaning we are "sojourners and pilgrims" whose "true home" is the "heavenly Jerusalem" (John 18:36; Philippians 3:20) [13, 26, 30, 31, 38, 142, 1226, 1313, 1320, 1426, 1529, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Treatment of Stateless Sojourners**

**Verse**
“ ‘You shall neither mistreat a stranger nor oppress him, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt’ ” (Exodus 22:21). [811, 1284, 1319, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture reveals that God "administers justice for the fatherless and the widow, and loves the stranger, giving him food and clothing" (Deuteronomy 10:18) [837, 1317, Conversation History]. The Reformed tradition emphasizes that the church must not "ape the world’s fads" of nationalism or prejudice, but instead "show every consideration for all men" because "there is no distinction between Jew and Greek" (Romans 10:12; Titus 3:2) [70, 118, 263, 1142, 1201, 1313, 1409, 1426, Conversation History]. Believers are called to "bear one another’s burdens" and "visit orphans and widows in their trouble," recognizing that "pure and undefiled religion" involves caring for those who have no earthly "provision or protection" (Galatians 6:2; James 1:27) [591, 904, 1128, 1202, 1317, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
"Never become so involved in this world" that you forget you are also a "sojourner with God," for "I am a stranger with You, a sojourner, as all my fathers were" (Psalm 39:12) [51, 130, 1031, 1503, 1623, Conversation History]. You must "discipline your mind" to "let your light so shine before men" by being "peaceable, gentle," and compassionate to the displaced, for "the Lord knows your hearts" (Matthew 5:16; Luke 16:15) [11, 77, 116, 321, 410, 680, 786, 1111, 1274, 1406, 1515, 1532, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, "cities of refuge" provided physical safety for those who were displaced by legal crises [733, 851, 1169, 1170, 1231, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** the concept of safety, revealing that we have "fled for refuge to lay hold of the hope set before us," an "anchor of the soul" that is not dependent on a physical border or a "national identity" (Hebrews 6:18–19) [4, 826, 937, 1235, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: Coercion of Identity vs. Spiritual Registry**

**Verse**
“ ‘And do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. But rather fear Him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell’ ” (Matthew 10:28). [11, 183, 1207, 1321, 1473, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—exemplified by **John Huss**—refused to let a human "aristocracy" define their spiritual identity, for "Christ alone is the Head of the church" [1528, 1536, 1636, 1720, Conversation History]. When the state attempts to "force a new liturgy" or coerce religious profession, it is a "spirit of fraud," for a believer’s "identity has been transformed" by the King who "purchased His people with His blood" (Acts 20:28) [30, 68, 102, 190, 243, 248, 1032, 1313, 1315, 1402, 1406, 1426, 1491, 1502, 1515, 1646, Conversation History]. No earthly "registration" can compare to being "registered in heaven," and therefore we "must obey God rather than men" (Acts 5:29; Hebrews 12:23) [612, 1130, 1144, 1163, 1168, 1218, 1255, 1256, 1316, 1321, 1426, 1431, 1529, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should "not be deceived" by a "no-lordship ideology" that seeks "deliverance" through political safety, for "your life is not your own" because you were "bought at a price" (1 Corinthians 6:19–20) [12, 91, 101, 1054, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. "Wait for His Son from heaven," knowing that "nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan" and your "true identity" is "hid with Christ in God" (1 Thessalonians 1:10; Colossians 3:3) [11, 21, 24, 94, 121, 201, 1032, 1132, 1143, 1315, 1408, 1515, 1572, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note**
In the ancient **context**, "adoption" of slaves gave them an "objective standing" and a "new name" in a family register [389, 390, 395, 244, 323, 327, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our "witness," showing that we are "children of God" and "joint heirs with Christ" through a "judicial declaration" that no "unrighteous judge" can revoke (Romans 4:6; 8:17) [14, 26, 112, 115, 315, 347, 348, 385, 387, 391, 404, 610, 611, 809, 861, 873, 880, 891, 1089, 1179, 1254, 1271, 1272, 1514, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Final Verdict on State Pride**

**Verse**
“ ‘God has numbered your kingdom and put an end to it.… You have been weighed on the scales and found deficient’ ” (Daniel 5:26–27). [37, 1061, 1402, 1720, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture handles the "noise and tumult" of "tyrannical" regimes by pointing to the "consummation of history," where "Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own" [13, 20, 24, 31, 103, 136, 1199, 1315, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. "Earthly kingdoms go the way of all flesh," and every "human monument" or "monument of pride" will "vanish—like smoke they vanish away" (Psalm 102:3) [11, 32, 37, 63, 789, 976, 1460, 1684, Conversation History]. Because the "Sovereign of the universe" "raises up kings" only to serve His "administration," no despot can truly "write himself into God’s office" without facing "perfect justice" at the "end of the age" [15, 835, 1143, 1315, 1532, 1533, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You can find "tranquility of soul" by "resting upon the surest foundation," knowing that "the Lord knows those who are His" and "His everlasting dominion" is "secure" (2 Timothy 2:19; Psalm 138:2) [11, 24, 25, 47, 92, 121, 147, 176, 201, 211, 222, 285, 300, 324, 352, 361, 405, 412, 414, 444, 591, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1408, 1420, 1441, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. "Wait for His Son from heaven," for He will "wipe away every tear from their eyes" and His "perfect kingdom" will never pass away (Revelation 21:4) [13, 14, 15, 24, 30, 31, 94, 109, 142, 201, 412, 470, 816, 822, 948, 1132, 1143, 1313, 1315, 1408, 1426, 1450, 1503, 1515, 1524, 1636, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“ ‘Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness” ’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 324, 361, 405, 414, 444, 591, 1138, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

references.cited_text: God commands His people to be holy (1 Peter 1:16), but only God Himself is actually holy. To pray “hallowed be Your name” is to attribute to God the holiness that already is, and has always been, supremely and uniquely His. To hallow God’s name is to revere, honor, glorify, and obey Him as the one and only completely perfect God. When we do, we remind ourselves of the important difference between us and Him. God lives in a different sphere than we do. He is holy and undefiled, but we are sinners. Only through His gracious provision of Jesus Christ and His payment for the penalty of our sin are we even able to approach Him. We agree with John Calvin, who said that God should have His own honor, of which He is so worthy, and that we should never think or speak of Him without the greatest veneration.3

Jewish people considered the Samaritans ethnically and religiously unclean—and the Samaritans likewise resented and despised their Jewish cousins. The Samaritans were descendants of Israelites who had intermarried with pagans after the Assyrians forced most of the population of Israel’s Northern Kingdom into exile in 722 BC (2 Kings 17:6). When the Assyrians conquered Israel’s Northern Kingdom, they carried away much of the population into captivity, and they purposely populated the land with expatriate pagans from other Gentile lands. “The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel; and they took possession of Samaria and dwelt in its cities. And it was so, at the beginning of their dwelling there, that they did not fear the Lord” (vv. 24–25).

For others, being a Christian is largely political, a quest to defend moral values in the public square or perhaps to preserve those values by withdrawing from the public square altogether. This new commitment, which is a commitment to righteousness (Rom. 6:19), holiness (1 Thess. 3:13), and newness of life (Rom. 6:4), finds expression in the description of Christians as Christ’s doúloi [slaves] (1 Cor. 7:22; Eph. 6:6).”13 Slaves of Christ are to be “always abounding in the work of the Lord” (1 Cor. 15:58), “trying to learn what is pleasing to the Lord” (Eph. 5:10), and ever seeking to “understand what the will of the Lord is” (Eph. 5:17).14 Rightly regarding themselves as “a people for His own possession, zealous for good deeds” (Titus 2:14), they obey the Word of God with eagerness.15 They understand and embrace the ethical implications of being a slave of Christ, knowing that “the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and His ears are open to their prayer, but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil” (1 Peter 3:12 NKJV). As a result, they pursue lives of holiness, longing to be fit for the Master’s service.16

Of course, those under Satan’s dominion will share his same demise of eternal destruction. Though sin promises satisfaction and life to its slaves, its reward is in actuality the exact opposite—misery in this life and condemnation in the next.20 The astonishing reality is that even if the sinner could change the condition of his heart—which Scripture teaches is impossible (Jer. 13:23)— no unbeliever would ever will to do so. Left to his own natural reason and volition, the unredeemed sinner will always choose slavery to sin over obedience to God. Until the Lord intervenes, the sinner is neither able nor willing to abandon his sin and serve God in righteousness. Both his will and his reason are utterly corrupt.
